sources.title: React Three Fiber v9.8.1 release
sources.evidence_summary: Release notes describe renderer disposal when Canvas unmounts and Activity/Suspense visibility handling, including keeping hidden Canvas roots alive and releasing them when actually removed.
sources.use_in_report: Stable R3F lifecycle update and hide-versus-unmount guidance

sources.title: React Three Fiber v9.8.2 release
sources.evidence_summary: Release notes describe portal root-state leak fixes, DPR updates on display/zoom changes, and correct removal behavior with frameloop demand; notes that dpr prop can override setDpr on Canvas rerender.
sources.use_in_report: Latest stable release evidence and memory/DPR/demand-loop recommendations

sources.title: React Three Fiber v10.0.0-alpha.6: Going WebGPU First
sources.evidence_summary: Documents WebGPURenderer as default, /legacy for GLSL/WebGLRenderer apps, @react-three/tsl split, multi-canvas renderer sharing, and fixed 1/60 physics phase timestep.
sources.use_in_report: WebGPU migration direction and alpha-only caveats

sources.title: React Three Fiber Canvas API
sources.version_or_scope: Current Canvas API documentation at retrieval
sources.evidence_summary: Documents fallback, error boundary guidance, sync/async renderer factories, WebGPURenderer initialization, and renderer ownership/disposal rules.
sources.use_in_report: Renderer ownership, fallback, and Canvas lifecycle

sources.title: WebGPU specification — devices and GPUDevice
sources.publisher: W3C GPU for the Web Working Group
sources.evidence_summary: Defines device ownership and invalidation, GPUDevice.lost promise, GPUDeviceLostInfo reason values, and implementation-defined message behavior.
sources.use_in_report: WebGPU device-loss semantics and resource invalidation

sources.title: HTMLCanvasElement: webglcontextlost event
sources.version_or_scope: MDN page last modified 2026-10-26; WebGL context event
sources.evidence_summary: Documents that webglcontextlost fires on the canvas and does not bubble; includes event registration and simulator example.
sources.use_in_report: Canvas event wiring and context-loss detection

sources.title: HTMLCanvasElement: webglcontextrestored event
sources.evidence_summary: Documents that old textures and buffers are invalid after restoration and application state/resources must be reinitialized.

sources.title: HTMLCanvasElement: webglcontextcreationerror event
sources.evidence_summary: Documents context creation failure event and platform-dependent statusMessage.
sources.use_in_report: No-context diagnostic and static fallback path

sources.title: WebGLRenderingContext: isContextLost()
sources.evidence_summary: Documents context-loss state check and causes including GPU contention, GPU switching, long GPU operations, and driver updates.

sources.title: Handling Lost Context in WebGL
sources.version_or_scope: Khronos WebGL wiki guidance; current page indexed at retrieval
sources.evidence_summary: Recommends preventDefault on context-lost event, stopping render loop, recreating all WebGL state/resources after restoration, and handling outstanding async asset loads.
sources.use_in_report: Detailed WebGL recovery sequence and QA strategy

sources.title: Three.js WebGPURenderer manual
sources.version_or_scope: Current manual at retrieval; npm semver not pinned
sources.evidence_summary: Documents WebGPU backend with automatic WebGL2 fallback, async renderer initialization, dispose method, forceWebGL testing option, and renderer limitations/migration notes.
sources.use_in_report: Three.js renderer boundary and public API limitations

sources.title: GPUDevice: lost property
sources.version_or_scope: Current MDN WebGPU API page; marked limited availability
sources.evidence_summary: Documents lost promise, transient loss causes, recreation of device-owned resources, and possibility that an adapter becomes unavailable.
sources.use_in_report: WebGPU loss recovery and bounded retry design

sources.title: Three.js WebGLRenderer API
sources.version_or_scope: Current API reference at retrieval; npm semver not pinned
sources.evidence_summary: Documents dispose(), forceContextLoss(), and forceContextRestore() as renderer methods; force methods depend on WEBGL_lose_context support.
sources.use_in_report: Expected teardown diagnostics and controlled context-loss testing

sources.title: Intersection Observer API
sources.evidence_summary: Documents asynchronous intersection callbacks, rootMargin, and use cases including lazy-loading content before it enters the viewport.
sources.use_in_report: Lazy mounting and prewarming the 3D scene

sources.title: Page Visibility API
sources.evidence_summary: Documents visibilitychange, hidden/visible states, and browser behavior such as pausing requestAnimationFrame in hidden tabs.
